references.text: Describes Phinehas' action when he took a spear and pierced the Israelite man and the Midianite woman, which is why God's wrath was turned away.
God declares Himself to be a jealous God, using the same word (קִנְאָה) that describes Phinehas' jealousy.
The Lord is called 'Jealous' (קַנָּא), and this verse shows that Phinehas shared God's jealousy.
Describes God as a consuming fire and a jealous God, explaining why God's wrath had to be turned away.
The psalm refers directly to Phinehas' action and how it was credited to him as righteousness.
Elijah uses the same expression about being zealous for the Lord, showing the same kind of holy zeal as Phinehas.
Elijah repeats his zeal for the Lord, an echo of Phinehas' jealousy.
Aaron stood between the living and the dead to stop the plague, similar to how Phinehas' action stopped God's wrath.
Paul speaks about zeal for God, linking to Phinehas' example of holy zeal.
Paul describes a divine jealousy (ζῆλος θεοῦ), which reflects Phinehas' zeal for God.
